_source: Where a state's contests this cycle do not follow its own calendar's one primary and a plurality November: a hand-maintained record of legal facts (AGENTS.md 3a), in two parts, each citing its law: `standing`, the law in force every cycle until it changes (a runoff date as the statute counts it, `runoffDaysAfter` the general), and `cycles`, the facts of one cycle only (a court-ordered or legislated one-off). Checked 2026-10-09. Georgia: O.C.G.A. 21-2-501(a)(1) requires a majority of the votes cast in a general election, else a runoff between the top two on the 28th day after (21-2-501(a)(5)): standing, so every cycle's runoff date is computed from its own general. Louisiana (2026 only): after Louisiana v. Callais the Legislature moved the 2026 U.S. House races to the fall open primary (Act 2 and HB 842, 2026 Regular Session; Secretary of State election calendar): every candidate, of every party, on one Nov 3 ballot, a majority winning the seat outright, else the top two in a Dec 12 runoff; its May 16 closed primary was the Senate's. Alabama (2026 only): the Governor postponed the primaries for U.S. House districts 1, 2, 6 and 7 to a special primary on 2026-08-11 after the 2023 map was reinstated (proclamation; Secretary of State special primary election), the other districts and the Senate keeping May 19. Top-two and top-four primaries, where every candidate of every party ran on one primary ballot and the leaders advanced to November whatever their party, so one party can hold both (or several) November places: California, Constitution art. II sec. 5 (Proposition 14, 2010), the top two; Washington, RCW 29A.52.112 (Initiative 872, 2004), the top two; Alaska, Alaska Stat. 15.25.100 (2020 Ballot Measure 2), the top four, November then decided by ranked choice (the ranked-choice fact itself is read from state_candidate_sources.json's ranked_choice_general, not repeated here). Edit it when a law changes or a cycle has a one-off; a cycle with no one-off needs no entry, and the standing rules still apply.
_use: Read by app/api/elections.py (_election_rules) into the state ballot's generalRunoffs, otherPrimaries and topPrimary. offices: 'S', 'H', or '*' for every contest on the ballot; districts: the House districts it covers, omitted for all. openPrimary: the November contest is itself an all-party primary, so several candidates of one party is the normal shape, not an error. topPrimary.advance: how many candidates the all-party primary sent to November. runoffDaysAfter: the runoff is that many days after the general (the date is computed per cycle and served as runoffDate).
